methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective DCE-MRI study of 221 subjects (74 HC, 78 LC, 69 LCBM) using 3T United Imaging UMR780 with Extended Tofts two-compartment modeling and defined ROI-based quantification in six white matter regions. Grouping criteria (LCBM maximum diameter <0.5 cm to exclude mass effect) and exclusion criteria are specified. However, methodological issues include: manual ROI delineation without reported blinding or inter-rater reliability; no matching of groups for age/sex; no adjustment for tumor stage, chemo/RT exposure, or smoking; the ADC vs SCC vs SCLC subgroup analysis has unreported sample sizes per subtype (Table 1 not directly visible); and no correction for multiple comparisons across 6 regions x 4 parameters x multiple subgroup contrasts. Statistical approach (Mann-Whitney U, Spearman) is adequate for the data type.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The hypothesis that non-metastatic lung cancer induces subtype-specific BBB permeability changes in cerebral white matter is translationally interesting and potentially relevant to brain metastasis risk stratification and cognitive/pain research in oncology. Proposed clinical thresholds (Ktrans >22, Ve >10) and therapeutic extensions (BBB protectants, osimertinib) are speculative and not validated in this study. Design is retrospective observational cohort, Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: As an observational imaging cohort, STROBE is the applicable standard; no explicit STROBE adherence is stated. IRB approval (KY2023073) with informed consent waiver is reported. DCE-MRI sequence parameters, ROI rules, and pharmacokinetic model are described in reasonable technical detail. Missing items include: per-group sample sizes for pathological subtypes, exact contrast agent dose (beyond rate), blinding of ROI placement, handling of motion-failed scans beyond exclusion, and any inter-observer reproducibility. No data availability or code sharing.

novelty_literature.justification: Using DCE-MRI to characterize BBB permeability in cerebral white matter stratified by lung cancer histopathology in a pre-metastatic population is a meaningful extension of prior work (Zhang 2022 on BBB leakage in non-metastatic LC and Xu 2020 on texture changes). The subtype-regional specificity (ADC global, SCLC deep white matter, SCC low) is a new angle but largely hypothesis-generating and biologically speculative in places.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is detailed and methodologically structured but highly verbose, with a very long Introduction and a sprawling Discussion that repeatedly restates the same core findings. Many passages are awkwardly phrased (likely translated), with run-on sentences. Tables and figures are referenced but Table 1 (group demographics and subtype counts) is not embedded, making validation difficult. The clinical recommendations section is overly prescriptive given the observational nature of the data.

key_strengths: Quantitative DCE-MRI with Extended Tofts modeling in 221 subjects across three well-defined groups (HC, LC, LCBM with metastases <0.5 cm)
Novel subtype-specific (ADC/SCC/SCLC) and region-specific analysis of BBB permeability in cerebral white matter
Clear clinical hypothesis linking paraneoplastic effects to pre-metastatic cerebral white matter BBB changes
Correlation analysis (Ktrans vs Vp) providing mechanistic differentiation between ADC/SCC (permeability-driven) and SCLC (interstitial-driven)
key_concerns: No correction for multiple comparisons across 4 parameters x 6 regions x multiple subgroup contrasts, raising false-positive risk
Groups not matched on age, sex, smoking status, or treatment exposure; potential confounding unaddressed
Manual ROI delineation without reported blinding or inter-rater reliability
Per-subtype sample sizes not embedded in the main text; SCC subgroup sample size may be small given reported 14.49% BM rate
No correlation with clinical cognitive or pain outcomes (MoCA, MMSE, VAS), as authors acknowledge
No data or code availability; STROBE not explicitly applied
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically adequate observational DCE-MRI study with novel but hypothesis-generating subtype-specific findings; fits a mid-tier oncology/neuroimaging journal after major revisions to add multiple-comparison correction, matching, and clinical-outcome correlation.
